 Connecticut early voter turnout so far; key races to watch 
 Among the key races, voters will be choosing their governor in this election. 
 By Jayne Chacko • 
 Published November 2, 2026 • 
 Updated 3 hours ago 
 BOOKMARKER 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 The total number of votes so far makes up about 22% of the state’s registered 2.2 million voters.
 Polls opened at 6 a.m. across the state for Election Day on Tuesday. For many in the state, they've already cast their ballot.
 So far, 513,321 voters have cast their ballots, with 455,016 people voting early and 58,305 returned absentee ballots, according to the Secretary of the State's office. 
 Stream Connecticut News for free, 24/7, wherever you are.
   WATCH HERE 
 Among those votes, 216,107 were registered Democrats and 89,115 were registered Republicans. Unaffiliated votes totaled 143,739 and 6,055 fell under the category of "other." 
 Comparing the numbers from 2022, another midterm year, voter turnout was at 57%, a drop from 2018’s turnout at 65%. Early voting was not available for these elections.
 The total number of voters for this year’s election will be released later this week. 
 Among the key races, voters will be choosing their governor in this election.
 Gov. Ned Lamont is running for a third term, and if he wins and stays in office for the next four years, he would be longest-serving governor in Connecticut's post-colonial, modern history. The current governor who holds that record is William O'Neill, who served from 1980 to 1991. 
 Lamont is touting his successes, like an income tax cut, budget surpluses, and more housing permits, while promising to lower costs for families. 
 "I think the state's come a long way over the last eight years, but we have some work to do," he said while campaigning Monday. "Make sure this place is affordable for everybody. Bring down the cost of healthcare.”
 Republican candidate State Sen. Ryan Fazio said he can do a better job at lowering taxes. He promised a tax cut of more than $2,000 per family over four years and to cut the cost of electricity. 
 "Our campaign is based on two things more than anything else: a love of our state and a belief that with a positive change it can succeed," Fazio said.

 Affordability, taxes and the economy are the top issues for voters in Connecticut and across the country. 
 A NBC News poll surveying 1,000 people said more voters say they are dissatisfied with their financial situation than satisfied, a first in the network's 30 years of polling.
 Those issues are also at the center of the races for Connecticut’s representatives.  
 In Connecticut's First Congressional District, former Hartford mayor Luke Bronin (D) is looking to secure his first term in Congress. He said he’ll focus on affordability and passing universal healthcare. 
 His challenger, Republican Amy Chai said Congress should trim debt and remove private equity from healthcare. 
 Bronin is hoping to keep the seat blue with the First District not electing a Republican to office since the late 1950s. Bronin beat long-term Rep. John Larson in the August primaries. Larson has held his seat for nearly 30 years, first elected in 1998. 
 In Connecticut's Fifth Congressional District, Rep. Jahana Hayes (D) said she’ll push back against Pres. Trump's cuts to Medicaid and SNAP while Republican candidate Chris Shea wants to make the tax cuts permanent. 
 Polls close at 8 p.m. Tuesday.  Same-day voter registration is allowed in Connecticut.  To find your same-day registration location, click here .
